correctness.rationale: Let \(Y=X\oplus A_r\) with all points of the antichain \(A_r\) above \(X\). If a fixed-point-free monotone map \(F:Y\to Y\) sent some \(x\in X\) to a new maximum \(a_j\), then monotonicity from \(x<a_i\) would force \(F(a_i)=a_j\) for every new maximum and in particular \(F(a_j)=a_j\), contradiction. Hence \(F|_X=g\) is a fixed-point-free endomorphism of \(X\). For fixed \(g\), the image of each new maximum \(a_i\) may independently be any common upper bound in \(X\) of \(g(X)\), giving \(u(g)\) choices, or any of the other \(r-1\) new maxima. No relation inside the antichain couples these choices. This gives exactly \((u(g)+r-1)^r\) extensions and summing over \(g\in\operatorname{Fpf}(X)\) proves the formula. The converse construction is immediate and proves exhaustiveness. The assigned verifier checks 265 labeled-poset instances, all \(r=2\) cases through four points and all \(r=3\) cases through three points; these computations are regression checks only because the symbolic extension bijection proves all finite \(X\).
residual_risks: The independent-choice factor is special to a cap that is an antichain of new maxima.

value.rationale: Non-Hausdorff suspension and ordinal sums are standard constructions in finite topology and poset theory. The theorem turns the known qualitative fixed-point-property behavior into an exact extension formula for every fixed-point-free base map and every cap size, isolating the natural common-upper-bound statistic. This is a concise structural lemma with reusable enumerative content rather than a small finite census.
residual_risks: Its usefulness is concentrated on this particularly simple ordinal-sum cap.
